key.name: appendages
key.summary: JSON array describing appendage workspaces in linear order.
key.description: Each entry: {"col": int, "dir": "up"|"down"}. The i-th entry corresponds to the workspace at linear index (main-row-size + i).

key.name: main-row-size
key.summary: Recorded size of the main horizontal row.

key.name: forget-empty-on-disable
key.summary: Forget empty appendages when the extension is disabled.

key.name: branched-indicator
key.summary: Render branches inside the native Activities preview.
key.description: When enabled (default), the GNOME Activities workspace dots are replaced with a 2D variant: the main row uses native dots (preserving scale/expansion animations) and small bars above/below each column represent vertical appendages. When disabled, falls back to a separate standalone panel indicator.

key.name: indicator-show-branches
key.summary: Show vertical branches in the indicator.
key.description: When the Activities indicator is in branched mode, controls whether vertical bars for appendages are shown. When disabled, only the main horizontal row is drawn — useful if you keep using vertical workspaces but prefer a clean, native-looking indicator.

key.name: window-rules
key.summary: JSON array of window-routing rules (fallback when no profile is active).
key.description: Each rule is an object {"match": {...}, "target": {...}}. Supported match fields (AND-combined): wm_class (exact), app_id (exact, gtk_application_id or sandbox_id), title (regex), pid_comm (exact, process name from /proc/<pid>/comm). Target: {"col": N, "layer": N, "create_if_missing": bool}. Optional "icon": icon for windows GNOME cannot map to a .desktop (e.g. Unity Editor, matched by pid_comm) — otherwise such windows get no icon in overview previews and alt-tab. Accepts a ".desktop" id (borrow that app's icon), an absolute path, or a themed icon name. Optional "name": display name for those same windows (defaults to wm_class). First rule that matches wins. Used when active-profile is empty or refers to a missing profile. Rules are owned by the user: the extension never rewrites this key (the main row grows to fit the columns rules ask for, not vice versa).

key.name: profiles
key.summary: JSON array of named profiles bundling rules + autostart.
key.description: Each profile: {"name": "Work", "rules": [...same as window-rules...], "autostart": [{"cmd": ["firefox"]}, {"cmd": ["code", "--new-window"]}]}. Autostart commands are spawned via Gio.Subprocess (argv array, no shell) when the active profile changes — or once per session if the extension loads and the active profile differs from the cached session profile.

key.name: active-profile
key.summary: Name of the currently active profile (empty = none).

key.name: drum-rotation
key.summary: Drum mode for vertical navigation.
key.description: When enabled, Super+Up/Down does not navigate to an appendage workspace. Instead, the active column rotates like a drum: the workspace at layer +1 (or -1) becomes the new main, and the previous main slides into layer -1 (or +1). The active workspace index always stays on the main row — only the workspace shown there changes. Mutter is reordered to keep linear indices consistent, so other extensions and AMW rules see the freshly-rotated arrangement.

key.name: pin-pip-windows
key.summary: Keep Picture-in-Picture windows on all workspaces, always on top.
key.description: When enabled (default), any window whose title looks like a Picture-in-Picture video (Firefox, Chrome/Chromium, …) is pinned to every workspace via the shell's "Always on Visible Workspace" and kept above other windows — so the floating video stays visible when you switch columns. Disabling stops pinning new PiP windows; already-pinned ones unstick when closed.

key.name: gesture-override
key.summary: Remap 3-finger touchpad gestures.
key.description: When enabled, 3-finger vertical swipe is captured for our vertical column navigation (with a smooth slide), and the overview / app-grid ladder is moved to 4-finger up/down. When disabled (default), the native GNOME 3-finger behaviour is left intact: 3-finger vertical opens the overview / app grid and 3-finger horizontal switches workspaces. Super+scroll and scroll-over-panel keep working either way.

key.name: switch-up
key.summary: Switch to workspace above current column.

key.name: switch-down
key.summary: Switch to workspace below current column.

key.name: switch-left
key.summary: Switch to workspace to the left within main row.

key.name: switch-right
key.summary: Switch to workspace to the right within main row.

key.name: move-window-left
key.summary: Move active window to the left within main row.

key.name: move-window-right
key.summary: Move active window to the right within main row.

key.name: create-up
key.summary: Create and switch to a new appendage above current column.

key.name: create-down
key.summary: Create and switch to a new appendage below current column.

key.name: extend-row-right
key.summary: Extend main row with a new column on the right.

key.name: extend-row-left
key.summary: Insert a new column to the left of the current one.
key.description: Inserts an empty main-row column at the current position; the current column and everything to its right shift right by one. Window-routing rules that target the shifted columns are reindexed automatically.

key.name: move-window-up
key.summary: Move active window to workspace above.

key.name: move-window-down
key.summary: Move active window to workspace below.

key.name: remove-current
key.summary: Remove current appendage workspace.
